I'll start off by saying I generally try to not review games so early, in this case it's kinda warranted.

Immortal gets a lot of things right, but it's blatantly obvious the devs are amateurs at this style of gameplay. The souls-like genre is a category of game that can either be done right, or you can make one design mistake and mess the whole flow of the game up.
The ladder is what happened with Immortal.

While the game is extremely fun and was the first game to do gun-souls, Toadman missed the mark pretty hard.
The game is grueling and will be for new players which is sad. Dark Souls is hard but leaves room for error, Immortal is harder but forces you to use its clunk and get used to it until you're comfortable zipping around while knowing where your character will end up.

While Immortal is unnecessarily difficult, the game pays you off even as you struggle. I have to give this to the devs. 
If you're finding it hard to get weapons, get decent drops, and deal with bigger enemies, push on and push hard. Immortal drops random weapons per certain kill amounts (I assume this is what causes the drops), this helps newer players out and gives them a reason to attempt to kill, die, respawn, and push harder again until something usable pops up.


If there's a spot where Immortal kinda lets me down the most it's definitely gotta be in the level design. The game has a ton of assets that can sometimes unfortunately make the game feel very same-y in a lot of places, this causes the game to feel rather drab and plain sometimes. It's not always like this though! Immortal's worlds do an amazing job at feeling new and vibrant when you pop into some of them, sometimes the random lighting around, the design, and the enemies spawn points culminate the world together in a way that makes everything feel rather refreshing.


If in the end someone were to ask me if this game was worth buying, what would I say?
If you want to try one of the first gun-souls experiences and are willing to learn to cope but strive to stay alive, go for it!

Then there's the people who are skeptical, I don't blame you.
At this point I'd say to hold off and wait until Toadman announces another Immortal as I feel this game could really use one to maybe freshen the experience and show off what they've refined.

Immortal is a great game but has things that make it clutch to its knees, this makes it hard to recommend. 
Once you see past its issues and find beauty in it or just something fun to play, maybe then consider it, not for $30 though.
Just buy remnant don't bother with this trash.

In my opinion, Immortal: Unchained is an underrated gem. It is not perfect by any means: it's not the prettiest game due to being made by around 20 people, it's not the most well balanced or fair, and the animations are probably the worst thing about the game due to the way it can impact the gameplay. But what the game lacks in those categories, it makes up for it in other ways. It has an unexpectedly interesting story and lore (which pays off very well in the ending), a ton of content, replay value, enemy variety, location diversity, satisfyingly unique combat, striking art design, and deep, meaningful RPG mechanics.

The game can be played very out of order if so desired, including the DLC, which I played extremely early despite being endgame. Each of the game's three planets (plus a few surprises) have complex, sprawling level design with shortcuts, branching paths, secrets, and mechanics that reward backtracking without forcing it. Before I unlocked fast travel, I delved into the DLC area at level 20-ish, and came out level 120-ish, so I was geared and ready to face the rest of the game after struggling and fighting tooth and nail for every inch of ground in the DLC.

Enemies that may appear unfair or even broken at first just require the right approach to fighting them (which usually involves the proper use of locking on or free aiming -- I played the game with a keyboard and mouse and found it a perfect fit), adding to the initial frustration that can put players off, as well as adding to the already steep learning curve, but it ends up encouraging a very unique play style that is really up my alley: dodging physical projectiles, managing stamina all the while, before firing back with shots to the enemy's weak point for larger enemies, or just unloading into weaker enemies. The game certainly has an adjustment period, but it is worth it.

Hitboxes are for the most part very accurate even if the animations themselves can be unpolished, where a certain enemy may be aiming their gun upward but the shots from it will shoot at a downward angle toward you. However this is merely an occasional visual error, as the enemy shots would move in the way they do regardless of whether their animation bugged out or not, so it's something that can be gotten used to if you get used to the enemy's rhythm and won't get thrown off by a bit of animation jank. It can also go the other way, too, where enemies may occasionally get stuck or unable to path to you, though this only happened I think three or four times in the entire game, which took me over 60 hours to finish (Steam says I have less time in it than I do since I played it offline a bit).

I highly recommend supporting the developers so hopefully they can provide another Soulslike third person shooter. I love Remnant: From the Ashes as well which is what encouraged me to finally play this game after it sat in my Steam library for a while. If you want a good Soulslike shooter and are willing to be patient, adapt and aren't afraid to play a game that isn't very well documented online, then I highly recommend Immortal: Unchained.

AWESOME GAME!!!


 Preliminary Review -  If you love those 'old-school' games that required skill, grinding and 'sticking through it'  with modern solid feeling characters and enemies you're going to love this!!!

 This game reminds me of those xbox 360 games that were fun, simple in concept yet required skill to master, (along with tons of upgradability both to your guy and your weapons)

 with a setting much like 'Too Human' (which was an awesome game by the way, and in fact much like this one is -- awkward and 'weird' at first, but then if you give it a chance it's one of the coolest games ever), 

 the graphics and 'feel' of the game are great, a bit wonky feeling at first but as you get 'used' to it it all the sudden 'clicks' and you realize how great it all is.

 This game has a very solid, weighty physics-based feel to it, because everything gives you tactile feedback, from the recoil of your weapons to the arms and legs that can be shot off the enemies to the enemies actually --Reeling Back from the Actual area You're Shooting them In !!!  -- 

 About time a game has that!!  (been waiting for that for years!!..)

 It's amazing how few people even mention this stuff in the reviews or forums,

 basically folks, if you're sick of games that feel 'cheap' and 'cardboard cut-out', you're going to love this.



 Yes it's brutally hard, yes it has some 'jank' elements to it, but overall it's freaking great, super hard but equally super rewarding.

 Note also, likewise to the 'old-school' (somewhat lol) difficulty and structure of much of it, it also allows you to 'grind' your guy to new and better heights.

 If you're sick of games that are so 'on-rails' that the 'meta' has been taken out of them  (the types that almost always give you the exact xp necessary for the stage, always at the right time nothing more nothing less etc), then you're going to love this game.

 It goes by a system of 'altars' that when you go to it saves, reloads your ammo, and gives you healing stims.

 What nobody's mentioning is that you can do that infinite number of times,  what most are talking about are the 'frustrating' aspects of how 'hard' the combat is,

 But -- Nobody Seems to Mention that the Altars are Infinitely Reusable !!!!! ---

 Folks, that means you can go off kill a bunch of enemies, till you used all your healing stims, are out of ammo and/or almost dead, and  just go back to the altar and heal up!!

 Then do it all over again!!

 What's the point?  the point is that since the game actually is 'fun' to play, to shoot at the enemies with the great looking, sounding and feeling guns, see them fall apart (much like Binary Domain in pieces as they get knocked around etc) , 

 then you can go shoot enemies over and over (since they respawn after going to an altar over and over) to get the 'bits' needed to level up your guys skills!!

 So far it seems to me that 'leveling' in this game isn't based on 'xp', but simply upgrading your guys traits, and you seem to be able to do that with bits without limit as long as you have the required bits, and again you can simply 'farm' bits to your hearts content!!

 That means folks, that you can build up your guy to awesome levels, and the supposedly 'frustratingly hard' game actually becomes not only much easier but super fun!!

 Cause the beauty of it is your guy has multiple traits he can level up, from ones that raise your guns damage modifier (all guns are affected by specific gun damage modifiers you can level up with bits) to health increases to stamina increases etc.

 So again, you are free to simply kill as many enemies as you want, get bits, use those bits to raise your guys traits, and using altars to 'reset' your health, stims and ammo, (and enemy respawns), you are free to do that over and over as much as you want.

 And YES, most definitely, in this game it's 'fun' to do cause of how physics and solid-feeling everything is.

 Compared to most games that have airy-fairy feeling guns and low-feedback on shooting enemies, the 'grinding' you can do in this one is actually fun and satisfying.

 (The shooting/ enemy damage feedback in this game is like Remnant from the Ashes, 'Defiance' (the shooter mmo) and Binary Domain put together, looks and feels absolutely fantastic )

 The setting is amazing in this game as well, stages feel 'realistic' (believable) and have a very 'other-wordly' look and feel to them.

 I barely played a few hours and I know I'll run into the hated 'sniping' issue (enemies hit you from far but you can't hit them, etc), the teleporting issue (enemies can teleport near/behind you etc), all those things I'm sure to hate,

 but otherwise this game is amazing and a much needed breathe of 'fresh' air, cause so many other games nowadays are crp and garbage.

 It's amazing one of the least popular games by sales turns out to be one of the best games I played for the longest time yet.

 Much like 'Too Human' it has a few strong flaws people downvote and unfortunately that means people get scared away and don't get to see how awesome it is in many other ways.


 (Note I purchased 'Remnant: From the Ashes' the same night as Immortal, and I actually like Immortal -Far- better!!   That's not to say that Ashes isn't good, or that Immortal is better 'overall', but that for my personality and preference Immortal is a game that 'grabs' me far more, but they are very similar in a lot of ways, with Immortal being 'better' for a more rpg, hand-crafted and brutally challenging experience, whereas Remnant is better for just 'zoning out' and enjoying a more relaxing (generally speaking) shooting experience, and has the coop element as well).

 I recommend both highly but especially Immortal if you want a seriously awesome 'solid' experience, especially relative to all the airy-fairy cookie-cutter shallow feeling games out there.

Gun Souls with a dark sci-fi theme.

Challenging, while not being too cheap.

If you like games like this then get it, it's way better than I expected it to be, though still a bit stiff and rough around the edges.
The game starts a little slow, but really opens up with the environments, weapons and some new enemies.

Overall, if I had to give it a numerical rating it would be about 7.5-8/10, and if you are on the fence seeing as the game has a mixed rating, ignore and buy it.
Better than Lords of the Fallen. Sure that's a low bar but as far as Dark Souls wannabes go this game is not bad.
